question_type: Change in Series I share of total savings-bond redemptions (percentage points) plus absolute change in Series I redemptions, 'March 2000' to 'March 2005', two-value bracketed output

opus_divergence.what_opus_did: Opus read 'March 2000'/'March 2005' as the March 2000 and March 2005 Bulletin issues (reading A). It took Table SBN-1, 'Sales and Redemptions by Series, Cumulative', from those issues; that table is cumulative through Dec 31 of the prior year. It used the Series I and Total rows of the Redemptions column. Opus listed two alternatives: (B) SBN-1 cumulative through Mar 31, from the June issues; and (C) monthly March flows from SBN-2 (all-series total) and SBN-3 (Series I), in first-print (C1) and latest-revision (C2) versions. It computed all four and chose A. Its reasons: the dates match issue names, SBN-1 is the one table listing each series with an all-series Total, and the question says neither 'cumulative' nor 'for the month of'. The key matches reading C2, which Opus computed and rejected. Both components of Opus's answer are far from the key (more than 25% off).
opus_divergence.what_right_glm_did: The cards arm read the dates as data months from the start ([21]: 'March 2000 data appears June 2000 issue'). It took the March rows from SBN-2 (all-series redemptions) and SBN-3 (Series I panel) in the June 2000 and June 2005 issues ([33]-[41]). It then scanned later printings for revisions ([42]-[58]). It found that the March 2005 all-series and Series I monthly cells were revised in the Sep 2005 through Mar 2006 issues, while the March 2000 cells were stable. It used the latest revision for each endpoint and computed the answer with a script ([58]-[61]).

reviewer_flag: Verdict CONFIRMED, with 'residual date-interpretation ambiguity' across readings A, B and C. The reviewer judged reading A (issue dates) 'the most likely intended one'. It said reading C 'requires going to other issues' and matches 'total redemptions (all series)' less naturally. So the reviewer argued against the keyed reading.
right_by_principled_choice_or_luck: Mixed. On vintage, cards was principled: it deliberately scanned every later printing and took the latest revision ([42]-[58]). No card covers savings bonds, so this echoes the 'latest issue printing' rule of C003/C007 in spirit. On interpretation, it was an unexamined default: cards took the data-month reading at [21] and never considered the issue-date reading (A) or the cumulative SBN-1 table (B). It got the interpretation right by not seeing the alternatives. Card C019 ('all series combined' trigger) only made it compute in a script. Note also that the prompt arm reached the identical candidate at [41]-[43] and then argued itself out of it.
wrong_glm_arms_same_as_opus: Partly. Prompt shared Opus's table preference but not its date reading. It first extracted the monthly flows, checked revisions, and computed the latest-revision candidate, which is the keyed reading ([35]-[43]). Then it ran a 'rule out an alternate reading' check ([44]) and switched to SBN-1 cumulative-by-series, dated 'through March 31' from the June issues. That is Opus's alternative B ([46]-[53]). Its reasoning echoes Opus's: a by-series table with an all-series Total is the natural source for a 'share', and 'from March 2000 to March 2005' reads as cumulative dates. Its first component matches Opus's; its second differs. None: no. It used the monthly-flow reading, like cards, with first-print values. For the March 2005 Series I value it read the next SBN-3 series panel, the Series E/EE block at 2005_06:2185 (per records/events.jsonl item_15), instead of the Series I block. That gave Series I an implausible share, most of all redemptions, which no check caught ([15]-[18]). This is a CELL_SELECTION error.
lesson_for_harness: This question is on the disputed list (issue47), so weight it lightly. Taking the key at face value, the intended reading is: a month named in the question is the data month, not the issue month; take the monthly flow rows; use the latest revision. Opus's 'dates match issue names' heuristic and the prompt arm's 'the cumulative by-series table fits share' heuristic both lost. Harness implications: (1) TEXT/STATE convention: 'Month-Year in a question = data period; the issue carrying it is later (June for March in the quarterly era); take the latest printing of that monthly cell.' (2) CONTROL: a late 'rule out alternatives' pass that has no decision rule can flip a correct candidate to a wrong one, as prompt did at [44]-[52]. Reconciliation needs an explicit precedence order, not a fresh judgment call. (3) CHECK: a plausibility bound on shares, which would catch the none arm's implausible share. The table-to-panel mix-up needs a panel-anchoring check that the series label heading the block is the series requested.
notes: Opus did the most complete enumeration: it computed the keyed value as option C2 and still chose otherwise. This is a pure interpretation/prior problem, not a search problem. Cards was the slowest arm (203 s, 29 requests) and prompt used about 2 M input tokens with a 137 KB AGENTS.md. The prompt adapter's conventions mention monthly-row vintage rules only for other tables (IFS-1 first printing; the prompt arm itself cited this at [43]), and it had no SBN lesson. Because the question is disputed, the official key may itself be wrong. The durable takeaway is about the control-flow flip in the prompt arm, not about which reading is 'right'.
